maintenance_cycle.notes: phase is DERIVED from immutable records; the C1/C2 admission binds a stored maintenance_stage_claim_set ROOT + pages (one page per batch, transitively claimed); COMPLETENESS: root.candidates (page concatenation) MUST equal expected_stage(role, freeze point) BYTE-FOR-BYTE — a strict subset, superset, wrong-role, or false-empty stage is refused at the C1/C2 admission fence; stage null iff expected_stage is empty (advances immediately). RESERVATION: the admission's irreversible-fence tx (COMPOSITE for P-credit, RECORD_PUT_ISSUED for P-less — round-20 A1) reserves every stage candidate for (cycle, role) — an ordinary prune intent naming a reserved candidate is refused STAGE_CANDIDATE_RESERVED; reservations release EACH AT ITS LINEARIZATION POINT — a CONFLICTED admission (different-winner proof) and a replacement CLEAR release in their named NONTERMINAL transactions (a losing attempt never produces a cycle terminal), while ABORTED_BEFORE_C1, replacement install, repair preemption, expiry, and completion release in that terminal's TERMINAL_APPLIED transaction; a candidate burned by an intent accepted BEFORE the freeze point is excluded from expected_stage (present = not burned). CYCLE-EVENT LANE (single linearization, org-slot lock): batch-completion acceptance, replacement arm/finalize/clear, repair preemption, and EXPIRED_STALLED terminalization all serialize in ONE lane; EXPIRED_STALLED may terminalize ONLY when now >= last_cycle_progress_at + 7 days AND no replacement fence is pending AND no cycle-tagged intent for this cycle is accepted without an accepted completion AND no completion is past its pre-I/O fence unresolved (the gateway, sole prune-lane writer, can always drive an accepted intent to a terminal, so the wait is bounded). PROGRESS: last_cycle_progress_at = max(effective_admitted_at of admissions with resource_binding.kind maintenance_cycle for THIS cycle — ordinary cycle_debit admissions are NOT progress, completed_at of every ACCEPTED cycle-tagged completed batch completion); each accepted completed batch resets it. TERMINAL EVIDENCE: every terminal publishes exactly ONE service-signed maintenance_cycle_terminal through the terminal_publication machine at the deterministic per-cycle key maintenance/terminals/<maintenance_cycle_id>.terminal.json; refusals of later cycle events begin at TERMINAL_PUT_ISSUED, and EVERY side effect (release, handoff, slot transition, accounting) applies only at TERMINAL_APPLIED — this machine's terminal STATES mean TERMINAL_APPLIED; the record is DR-authoritative over late-visible objects. EXPECTED-STAGE / GC-ROOT RECONCILIATION — SINGLE SOURCE: the checkpoint-recovery-bundle rule (round-13 A1). protected_after_C1 = RB(K1) UNION RB(K0) UNION later_receipts; protected_after_C2 = RB(K2) UNION RB(K1) UNION later_receipts; expected_stage(role) = universe MINUS protected(role). Nothing else — RB(K) is defined ONLY by that rule (claim set + manifest + all packs + K's covers_through ref_state + retention_roots). checkpoint_role C1 <=> role intermediate, C2 <=> role final (biconditional). RESERVATION RELEASES — each classified by its linearization point: a CONFLICTED C1/C2 admission (different-winner proof) and a replacement CLEAR release in their named NONTERMINAL transactions; ABORTED_BEFORE_C1, replacement install, repair preemption, expiry, and completion release ONLY inside that terminal's TERMINAL_STORED -> TERMINAL_APPLIED transaction. STAGE CAPACITY: every admission that could enlarge the future stage preflights BOTH candidate_count <= MAX_STAGE_CANDIDATES AND projected stage_candidate_stored_size_bytes <= MAX_STAGE_CANDIDATE_STORED_BYTES (MAINTENANCE_STAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) — the coverage-preflight precedent. REPAIR-ARM PRECEDENCE (round-12 A4): the repair fence ARM is itself an org-slot lane event validated against the expected open cycle (the binding's preempted_maintenance_cycle_id); a pending replacement DEFERS the repair arm until installed/cleared, and a pending repair fence defers the replacement arm — the two fences are mutually exclusive, so both records can never win against different vaults. MAINTENANCE-CYCLE-ID NON-REUSE (round-13 A2): maintenance_cycle_ids are SERVICE-ISSUED at cycle open, org-global, and permanently tombstoned — reuse is refused before any lease, stage object, or admission reaches a fence (the terminal path and event-seq namespace are never reused). ADMISSION FENCES IN THE LANE: see cycle_admission_fence. EVERY terminal-target edge above states its SOURCE predicate only: the named terminal state is reached, and ALL effects (release, handoff, accounting, installation, prune-eligibility) occur, solely when that cycle's terminal publication reaches TERMINAL_APPLIED. maintenance_admission_cut_subfence.notes: P-credit admissions use ONE COMPOSITE ADMISSION FENCE (round-20 A1): under the org-slot/cycle lane, EVERY fallible admission check runs FIRST — generation + head linkage, request-to-C1 equality, expected-stage equality + stage reservation, current cycle/terminal/repair/replacement predicates, cutoff + authorization epoch, generation/rate reservation, maintenance lease + quota; THEN prepared_at, the service-key authority, the signature, the exact admission-record bytes, AND the exact cut bytes are fixed; ONE transaction atomically persists both journals, claims the cut, reserves the stage, and enters BOTH CUT_PUT_ISSUED and CYCLE_ADMISSION_PENDING. AFTER that transaction no semantic validation may refuse — the remaining path is mechanical no-fail replay: CUT_PUT_ISSUED -> CUT_STORED -> RECORD_PUT_ISSUED -> RECORD_WON | CONFLICTED -> COMMITTED. The record's service signature attests THIS composite validation for P-credit admissions (RECORD_PUT_ISSUED's for P-less); authority time freezes at the admission's irreversible fence — composite for P-credit, main for P-less. P-less admissions keep the ordinary main fence and skip this machine. UNBOUND-CUT EXITS are exactly two: CONFLICTED (different-winner proof releases the cut to the reaper) and DR_ORPHANED_PRE_RECORD. DR: a scan-visible cut with NO recovered composite journal and NO canonical record binding it, after the quiescence wait and second scan, is DR_ORPHANED_PRE_RECORD — reconstruct an inert lifecycle row, release claims/reservations, FINALIZED_UNCLAIMED, reap; a canonical record binding it -> adopt; a different generation winner -> reconstruct CONFLICTED and release. The cut object does not carry the record bytes, so a lost journal can never resume the record PUT — orphan adjudication is the total answer.
